Summary
This letter, written by a family member to Jack, discusses the arrival of a letter and various items sent from Australia, including photos, newspapers, and magazines. The sender expresses joy at the items received and mentions Jack's new interest in golf. The letter also updates Jack on the family's situation, including the transfer of Abe, a family member, and mentions false alarms about Abe's picture appearing in the newspapers. The tone is warm and nostalgic, with a focus on family life and the sender's appreciation for the items received.

--- Page 1 (Beckerman_10a) --- Dear Jack, Your letter of 28 Jan arrived this week in addition to the envelope containing those fine fotos of Brisbane which we really enjoyed studying. To top off the armchair sight seeing tour there were the newspapers and Yank magazine, which came through the 1 month trip in tip top condition... Thanks for ace the stuff. Seeing newspapers that we can read; pictures of bridges and streets that might even be pictured in the American scene, all make Australia seem much closer and not so far enough away to be 'bleating hat' there and whipping coed here. He were glad to hear you've added another sport to your list. Golf seems a bit tame next to the surfboard and horseback riding, but the variety should make for a nice combination. The word 'Golf' serves to stir certain memories of such a course. Winter snow, golfing, and the 'green' are all invocations. Glen loves the idea of yachts & sea here. I was there were fancy white stones --- Page 2 (Beckerman_10b) --- gentle slopes - all of which have now degenerated to a convenient 'short cut'. We're still in the 'know-nothing' stage concerning Abe and are anxiously awaiting news as to where he has been transferred to. With so much more of the Philippines being liberated the possibilities of a new location likewise increase - But there's no large degree of worry attached as we know he is likely to be stationed in a safe area. Everything here is going in very usual order except for the semi-annual fish tank cleaning which is to take place tonight - all floor space between bedroom and bathroom is bedecked with a protective covering of newspaper Mama is determined not to lose a single specimen down the drain this time. Personalities in the news here contain the usual friendly familiar faces. Reena is still making off ananasanas as "Oh dad are you apples, hey guys we re-rile train Reena translating uves pclave into words... ..... And Sam is here each Sunday. --- Page 3 (Beckerman_10c) --- but instead of counting his money as he used to - its now his packs of cigarettes. Smoking was always his favorite pastime and the shortage him hard until he learned the knack of getting at the end of the line again and again, as he describes: Once with his hat on, s then off. Watching him take a pack out of lack pocket, count and fumble there makes us all laugh and forget that he's not doing just what is being urged now - volunt ary rationing! Of late we've had a number of false alarms concerning people reporting peeing yours and Abe's pictures in the papers. The second time Abe was 'mistakenly discovered' came to light the other night when Sarah called up excitedly telling us that Abe's picture was on the back page of the Daily News. He found it and saw the resemblance, but the '13 Army Air Force' heading didn't justify a resemblance. . . . Yesterday Abe's name appeared on the cover of a magazine on the back page. Magazine covers are that's supposed to resemble you. --- Page 4 (Beckerman_10d) --- He examined it from all angles and everyone finds another feature slightly familiar but the general agreement was -No, it ain't you- Papa is feeling all right but will be home next week. That could easily be foretold when he 'took the scissors out of his pocket' - bringing the scissors home is the sign of a workless week. Just when we all thought we were enduring the last plushy snow of the season - another came down yesterday covering all with a blanket of white. This certainly is the profoundest winter we've had in a long time! Well, we've about used up our quota of ink, paper, & words for today so we will be closing with Regards from all Love Mum Papa Ruth
